paraphrase: These (six) categories are enumerated as the principal ones; absence, though it has its own nature, is not enumerated because its determination depends on the determination of its counterpositive — not because it is a mere nothing.
notes: Quoted as the Kiraṇāvalī's statement in the modern commentary of the local Bhāṣāpariccheda e-text; location within the Kiraṇāvalī not checked.

location.ref: verse on the impediments to a universal (location not checked)

paraphrase: Six impediments exclude a genuine universal: the individual being only one; two terms having exactly the same extension; cross-division (saṅkara); infinite regress; loss of (the thing's) own nature; and absence of the relation (of inherence).
notes: Verse 'vyakter abhedas tulyatvaṃ...' recalled from memory; attribution to the Kiraṇāvalī is the usual one.
